notes: Evidence strengths: platform-official = published by YouTube/Google/TikTok/Meta (often correlational or modelled, and self-interested); experimental = controlled or field studies in peer-reviewed venues; observational = correlational data; practitioner = creator/agency guidance. rules[].heuristic=true means no source gives that number. Genre ranges reference results/benchmarks.json (n~6 videos per genre, descriptive only, not linked to outcomes).

parameters.name: Hook: visual change in the opening seconds
parameters.summary: Google's ABCD guide recommends more than two frames (shots) in the first five seconds, surprising visuals and tightly framed people/product at the start; TikTok says the opening 2-6 s carry most ad-recall impact. YouTube's 'intro' metric (share still watching at 30 s) is the official yardstick for long-form openings.

rules.note: ABCD: 'Have more than two frames in the first five seconds' (Awareness, Consideration). Count shot starts with t < 5 s, including the first shot.
ABCD threshold transferred from ads to organic content; untested outside ads.
Opening at least as visually active as the rest of the video. No source gives a number.
Compare to the genre's corpus p25-p75 in results/benchmarks.json (descriptive, n~6 per genre).

flags.description: Opening shot runs too long with little motion
flags.rule: First shot lasts > 5 s AND motion in that shot is below the video's median motion (heuristic; ABCD basis for ads).

flags.description: People are in the video but not in the opening
flags.rule: face visible somewhere in the video (face_share > 0.2) but not in any 0-3 s segment. ABCD: 'If your video features people, open with them on-screen.'

genre_notes.ad: Apply the ABCD rule directly: >2 shots in first 5 s, tightly framed person/product, surprising visual.
genre_notes.shorts: TikTok: first 2 s reportedly carry ~50% of ad impact and first 6 s ~90% of recall impact (ad data). Treat the first 1-2 s as the swipe decision.
genre_notes.vlog: A slower atmospheric open is common; compensate with a spoken/text promise within a few seconds (see clear_promise_early).
genre_notes.explainer: A talking-head open is fine if the question/promise is stated immediately.
genre_notes.tech_review: Open on the product close-up or the verdict tease.
genre_notes.cooking: Open on the finished dish (payoff preview) rather than ingredients.

parameters.name: Clear promise / value proposition early
parameters.summary: TikTok advises introducing the content proposition in the first 3 s and the hook within 6 s; YouTube says a weak intro (first 30 s) often means the opening does not match what the title/thumbnail promised. Curiosity-gap theory (Loewenstein 1994) explains why an explicit open question holds attention.

rules.note: TikTok: 'Introduce your content proposition in the first 3 seconds'. Detected from transcript words / on-screen text in hook beat.
YouTube only defines the 30 s intro window; 15 s is our heuristic to leave room before the 30 s checkpoint.
Hook story beat should contain a question, a stated outcome ('by the end you'll...'), or a payoff preview.

flags.description: No stated promise or question in the opening
flags.rule: No question mark, outcome statement or payoff preview in transcript/on-screen text before 15 s (long-form) or 3 s (short-form).

flags.description: Intro/setup runs long before the main content
flags.rule: Setup story beat ends after 30 s (long-form) or after 20% of runtime (short-form). Heuristic.

genre_notes.explainer: State the question being answered in the first sentence.
genre_notes.tech_review: Tease the verdict or the one surprising finding up front.
genre_notes.cooking: Show the finished dish and say what makes this recipe different.
genre_notes.vlog: Say where we are going / what happens today.
genre_notes.shorts: Promise must land in 1-3 s, usually as on-screen text plus first line.
genre_notes.ad: Proposition in first 3 s (TikTok); brand rules are separate (brand_timing).

parameters.name: Time to first voice / cold-open dead air
parameters.summary: ABCD notes that having people on-screen speak directly to the audience can help in the opening. No platform gives a numeric limit on silence before the first word; the threshold here is a heuristic.

rules.note: Heuristic. Corpus medians: explainer 0.0 s, tech_review 0.0 s, ad 0.7 s.
Heuristic; acceptable if on-screen text and motion carry the hook instead.
No threshold: vlog corpus median is ~17 s (music-led cold opens). Flag only if the opening also lacks text and motion.

flags.description: Silence or music-only before first word
flags.rule: time_to_first_word_s > genre threshold AND no on-screen text in the same window.

genre_notes.vlog: Music-led cold opens are normal; pair with text or strong motion.
genre_notes.cooking: Sizzle/ASMR audio can substitute for voice if it starts at 0 s.
genre_notes.ad: Voice or sound cue from frame one; ABCD favours on-screen speakers over plain voice-over for brand mentions.
genre_notes.shorts: Voice, text or a loud sound from frame one.

parameters.name: Pacing (cut rate and shot length)
parameters.summary: Cutting et al. (2011) measured Hollywood average shot length falling from ~10 s (1930s-40s) to <4 s after 2000 alongside more motion, and argue this reflects filmmakers' control of attention; this is descriptive, not causal, and film-specific. ABCD lists pacing among the opening levers. No source gives a causal optimum cut rate for online video.

rules.note: Use the genre's p25-p75 from results/benchmarks.json (corpus medians: ad 33, tech_review 12.6, shorts 12.7, explainer 10.2, vlog 7.9, cooking 5.0). Descriptive reference, not an outcome-validated target.
Same corpus-range approach. Report median not mean (skewed distributions).
Heuristic: a second half much slower than the first (ratio < 0.8) can feel like the video is running out of steam.

flags.rule: A shot longer than max(3 x genre median_shot_s, 8 s) with no format change, on-screen text change or speech-topic change inside it. Heuristic.
Rolling 30 s cut rate drops below 50% of the video's own median cut rate for > 30 s. Heuristic.

genre_notes.ad: Fastest genre in our corpus (median shot ~1.35 s).
genre_notes.cooking: Slowest; long process shots are expected - vary angle/close-ups rather than cutting faster.
genre_notes.explainer: Pacing is carried by speech and graphics as much as by cuts.
genre_notes.vlog: Moderate; long takes acceptable when something is happening.
genre_notes.tech_review: Interleave talking head with product b-roll.
genre_notes.shorts: Fast but not necessarily the fastest; text and motion carry pace.

sources.title: Cutting, Brunick, DeLong, Iricinschi & Candan, Quicker, faster, darker: Changes in Hollywood film over 75 years. i-Perception 2(6):569-576

parameters.name: Visual variety / pattern interrupts
parameters.summary: Guo et al. (2014, 6.9M MOOC sessions) found videos interspersing the speaker's talking head with slides were more engaging than slides alone. MrBeast's production document (practitioner) stresses re-engaging viewers so they don't 'get bored ... and click off'. Thresholds for 'too long without change' are heuristics.

rules.note: Genre p25-p75 from benchmarks.json (corpus medians: tech_review 5.1, ad 3.1, explainer 2.1, vlog 2.1, cooking 1.7, shorts 1.0).
Heuristic: avoid a single format (e.g. only talking head or only slides) for nearly the whole video, per Guo et al.'s talking-head + slides finding.
Heuristic: slides-only is the weakest format in Guo et al.

flags.description: No visual change for too long
flags.rule: No cut, format switch, or on-screen text change for > 8 s (long-form) or > 3 s (shorts/ad). Heuristic.

flags.description: Same format for a long stretch
flags.rule: Same on-screen format (talking head / b-roll / screen / text) uninterrupted for > 60 s in long-form. Heuristic.

genre_notes.explainer: Mix speaker and visuals (Guo et al. finding is from educational video, the closest genre).
genre_notes.tech_review: Alternate talking head, product b-roll and screen/benchmarks.
genre_notes.cooking: Variety comes from angle changes and close-ups of the process.
genre_notes.vlog: B-roll cutaways break up long talking stretches.
genre_notes.ad: Already high-variety by default; check for stalls on the end card.

parameters.name: Dead air (long pauses, low speech coverage)
parameters.summary: No platform publishes a pause threshold. Guo et al. found engagement generally rose with speaking rate, which argues against slack delivery in talk-led formats. YouTube's dips report shows where viewers skip or leave, which creators can line up with pauses. The 1.5-2 s thresholds are heuristics.

rules.note: Heuristic. Corpus medians: explainer 0.0, tech_review 0.08.
No threshold: pauses filled by music, ambient or process audio are normal here. Only flag silent pauses (see flags).
Heuristic for talk-led formats.

flags.rule: A gap > 2 s between words before 15 s with loudness below -45 dBFS (no music/SFX) and no on-screen text. Heuristic.
A gap > 1.5 s between words where audio is near silent (< -45 dBFS) AND no cut/format change occurs in the gap. Heuristic.

genre_notes.explainer: Trim breaths and 'umm' gaps; jump-cut pauses.
genre_notes.tech_review: Trim pauses; cover thinking time with b-roll.
genre_notes.cooking: Process audio (sizzle, chopping) counts as non-dead air.
genre_notes.vlog: Ambient/music pauses are part of the format; silent ones are not.
genre_notes.shorts: Any silent second is costly at this length.
genre_notes.ad: Every second is paid; pauses should be intentional beats.

parameters.name: Speaking rate and delivery energy
parameters.summary: In Guo et al. (2014) speaking rates ranged 48-254 wpm (mean 156) and, within a length bucket, engagement usually increased (up to 2x) with speaking rate; the authors recommend coaching enthusiasm and not slowing down deliberately. Evidence is from educational video only.

rules.note: Guo et al. mean was 156 wpm with engagement rising with rate; 150 is our heuristic floor, not a published cut-off. Corpus medians: tech_review 176, explainer 152.
Hook should not be slower than the body (compare hook_wpm to wpm). Heuristic.
No evidence-based target; music-led formats legitimately have low wpm (corpus vlog 55, shorts 67).

flags.rule: Rolling 30 s wpm in talk-led sections falls below 110 wpm (heuristic) while speech is present.

genre_notes.explainer: Closest match to Guo et al.'s setting; faster, enthusiastic delivery is supported.
genre_notes.tech_review: Fast delivery is the norm (corpus median ~176 wpm).
genre_notes.cooking: Instruction pace must match the action on screen; do not optimise wpm alone.
genre_notes.shorts: Often text/music-led; applies only to talking Shorts.
genre_notes.ad: Driven by script length; check legibility rather than speed.

parameters.name: On-screen text and captions
parameters.summary: TikTok's creative best practices recommend captions or text overlays for context and about 5-10 words per second when using text (official page, retrieved via search snippets). Meta guidance on captions for Reels could only be found in third-party summaries. ABCD recommends audible and visible CTAs and offers (text cards).

rules.note: TikTok recommends captions/text overlays; first-3 s timing is our application of the 3 s proposition guidance.
Heuristic for long-form (feed previews may play muted).
Genre p25-p75 from benchmarks.json; no source gives a target share.

flags.description: No on-screen text in first 3 s
flags.rule: hook_text_overlay is false for shorts/ad.
Promise, verdict, offer or CTA is spoken but no on-screen text appears within +/-2 s. Heuristic (ABCD 'audible and visible').

genre_notes.shorts: Text overlay in the first frame is the strongest-supported practice.
genre_notes.ad: Make offer and CTA both audible and visible (ABCD).
genre_notes.cooking: Ingredient quantities and steps as text (corpus median text share 0.81).
genre_notes.tech_review: Show specs, prices and the verdict as text.

parameters.name: Audio presence and energy arc
parameters.summary: TikTok-commissioned Kantar research (2021) reports 88% of users say sound is essential to the TikTok experience (survey, platform-funded). ABCD names audio among the opening levers. Cutting et al. speculate that faster cutting and motion raise arousal. No source gives loudness or energy-slope targets; all thresholds are heuristics.

rules.note: Heuristic sanity range; corpus p25-p75 is about -24 to -17. Platforms normalise playback loudness, so very quiet masters mainly lose clarity.
Heuristic: flag only strongly falling energy across the video.
Compare to genre corpus range; very low range can mean monotone delivery, very high range can mean inconsistent mix.

flags.rule: Loudness falls > 6 dB below the running 30 s median for > 3 s while speech or music is expected. Heuristic.
Mean loudness over 0-3 s is > 6 dB below the video's mean. Heuristic.

genre_notes.shorts: Sound is part of the format on TikTok/Shorts; music or a sound hook from frame one.
genre_notes.vlog: Music beds carry energy (corpus non-speech share ~0.65).
genre_notes.ad: Sound cue with brand (ABCD: audio mentions from on-screen people are more impactful than plain voice-over).
genre_notes.explainer: Clean, even voice; low music bed.
genre_notes.tech_review: Clean voice; avoid long music-only stretches.

rules.note: Direction from ABCD/TikTok; no numeric target published. Compare to genre corpus range.
Heuristic proxy for second-person address; no source gives a target. Corpus median 1.1.
Heuristic proxy for audience engagement and curiosity gaps (Loewenstein).

flags.description: Hook does not address the viewer
flags.rule: No 'you/your' and no question in the first 15 s of a talk-led video. Heuristic.

parameters.name: Re-engagement beats / payoff spacing
parameters.summary: YouTube advises that if top retention moments come late, move compelling content earlier, since audiences shrink over a video. MrBeast's production document (practitioner, leaked 2024) calls the first minute the most important and describes re-engaging the viewer around minutes 3 and 6. No study gives an optimal interval.

rules.note: Practitioner (MrBeast minute-3/minute-6 re-engagement); interval is our heuristic.
Not applicable: the whole video is one beat.

flags.description: Long stretch without a new beat
flags.rule: Long-form: > 180 s within the main story beat without a payoff, reveal, question, new segment or format change. Heuristic.
First payoff beat starts after 70% of runtime with no earlier preview of it. Heuristic based on YouTube's 'move compelling content earlier' advice.

genre_notes.tech_review: Spread findings; do not save every test result for the end.
genre_notes.explainer: Answer sub-questions as you go; tease the next one.
genre_notes.vlog: Plan an event or reveal every few minutes.
genre_notes.cooking: Intermediate reveals (sauce done, first taste) act as beats.

parameters.name: Emotional arousal (shareability)
parameters.summary: Berger & Milkman (2012) found content evoking high-arousal emotions (awe, anger, anxiety) was more likely to be shared and low-arousal sadness less so. Tellis et al. (2019) found amusement, excitement, inspiration and warmth increased video-ad sharing, while information-focused content reduced it (except in risky contexts); drama elements (surprise, plot, characters) helped. Our pipeline cannot measure emotion directly; signals are weak proxies.

rules.note: Look for at least one high-arousal peak (surprise/reveal/laugh) via perception model plus loudness/motion peaks. Proxy only; not validated.
Weak proxy for dynamic, arousing delivery. No source links this measure to sharing.

flags.rule: No moment where loudness AND motion both exceed their 90th percentile, and no surprise/reveal beat labelled by perception. Heuristic proxy.

genre_notes.ad: Tellis et al.: emotional, drama-led ads are shared more than information-led ones on general platforms.
genre_notes.explainer: Information-led content is shared less per Tellis; add awe/surprise in the framing.
genre_notes.tech_review: Surprise findings and strong verdicts are the arousal levers.

parameters.name: Brand timing and prominence (ads)
parameters.summary: Trade-off. ABCD: introduce the brand in the first five seconds for ad recall (awareness) using visual or audio cues. Tellis et al. (2019): early, long or persistent brand placement hurt sharing. Teixeira et al. (2010): pulsing brand exposure (intermittent) reduced zapping vs. the same total exposure shown continuously. Our pipeline does not detect logos; brand presence must come from transcript brand-name matches or the perception timeline.

rules.unit: s (brand first visible or audible by)
rules.note: ABCD (recall goal). Requires brand name from the user or a perception label.
Prefer intermittent (pulsed) brand appearances over a persistent one (Teixeira et al. 2010; Tellis et al. 2019 for sharing).

flags.rule: First brand mention/visual after 5 s in an ad optimised for recall.
Brand visible > 80% of runtime or continuously from 0 s; may hurt sharing (Tellis) and raise zapping vs pulsing (Teixeira).

genre_notes.ad: Pick the goal: recall (brand by 5 s) vs. sharing (lighter, later, pulsed branding).
genre_notes.tech_review: Sponsored segments: not covered by these sources.
genre_notes.cooking: Product placement: not covered by these sources.
genre_notes.shorts: For Shorts ads, TikTok's 3 s proposition guidance also applies.

parameters.name: Call to action: clarity and timing
parameters.summary: ABCD (Direct): a strong CTA is specific ('visit site', 'sign up', 'buy now') and is more effective when both audible and visible; urgency ('limited') works. No official source gives CTA timing for organic videos; any early-CTA rule is a heuristic.

rules.note: ABCD: direct viewers to take action.
CTA should be both audible (transcript) and visible (on-screen text) - ABCD.
Heuristic: avoid asking (subscribe/like) before delivering any value. No source found.

flags.description: Ad has no call to action
flags.rule: cta_count == 0 for genre ad.
CTA detected in transcript with no on-screen text within +/-2 s (ABCD 'audible and visible').
Subscribe/like/follow CTA within the first 15% of runtime of long-form content. Heuristic.

genre_notes.ad: Specific, audible + visible, ideally with urgency (ABCD).
genre_notes.shorts: A long outro CTA can break the loop (see loop_ending).
genre_notes.cooking: Recipe link CTA after the reveal.
genre_notes.vlog: End-of-video CTA is the norm (corpus median position 0.94).

parameters.name: Length fit for genre and platform
parameters.summary: Guo et al. (2014): shorter educational videos were much more engaging; they recommend chunks under 6 minutes. Tellis et al. (2019): ad sharing peaked at moderate length, 1.2-1.7 minutes. Wistia (vendor, 2020) reports the early drop-off grows with length: 4.9% of viewers lost in the first 2% of 1-2 min videos vs 17.3% for 5-10 min videos. YouTube Shorts may be up to 3 minutes (since Oct 2024). These are observational and context-specific; YouTube's own guidance is about retention, not length.

rules.note: Tellis et al.: sharing peaked at 1.2-1.7 min ad length (sharing goal only; recall-driven bumper/15 s ads differ).
Guo et al. (<6 min chunks) is MOOC data; applying it to YouTube explainers is an extrapolation.
YouTube Shorts maximum length (platform limit, not an optimum).
No source supports a target; use genre corpus range and judge by retention signals instead.

flags.rule: duration_s outside genre p10-p90 of corpus, or > 180 s for shorts. Heuristic except the Shorts limit.

genre_notes.ad: Sharing goal: ~1.2-1.7 min (Tellis). Recall goal: brand by 5 s matters more than length.
genre_notes.explainer: Chunk into < 6 min segments or chapters (Guo).
genre_notes.shorts: Hard limit 3 min on YouTube; shorter makes loops cheaper.

parameters.name: Ending and loop (short-form)
parameters.summary: Since 31 March 2025 YouTube counts a Shorts view when a Short starts or replays (the previous metric was renamed 'engaged views'), and replays add watch time; third-party analytics guides note average percentage viewed can exceed 100% on loops. No official source recommends designing seamless loops; this is practitioner advice and the thresholds are heuristics.

rules.note: Heuristic: last 1-2 s should not be a static end card, silence or 'thanks for watching'; ideally visually/audio continuous with the first frame.
Long-form: avoid long outros after the payoff (dips after payoff are common in YouTube's retention report).

flags.rule: Shorts: final 2 s are silent (< -45 dBFS) or a static frame (no motion) or an end card. Heuristic.
Long-form: > 20 s between the end of the payoff beat and the end of the video. Heuristic.

genre_notes.shorts: End on the punchline/reveal; cut immediately; consider matching last and first frames.
genre_notes.ad: End card with brand + CTA is expected (ABCD) - loop logic does not apply to ads.
